tests.notes: bool + uint8 + bool + address (1+1+1+20 = 23 bytes) declared sequentially all share slot 0 at offsets 0, 1, 2, 3
a uint256 always starts a fresh slot even when the previous slot has free bytes, and the variable declared after it starts yet another slot

a variable that does not fit in the remaining space of the current slot moves to the next slot; solc never splits one value across two slots (two uint128 exactly fill slot 0, uint256 takes slot 1, next uint128 takes slot 2)
struct fields pack among themselves, but the struct always starts at a fresh slot and the state variable declared after it also starts at the next fresh slot, so neither shares a slot with the struct
uint8[4] packs all four elements into a single slot; 1D counterpart of multidimensional/009
dynamic arrays and mappings each take their own base slot (length slot / unused slot) and never pack with neighbouring small variables; the next small variable starts a new slot
same variables as 001 in a different order: total bytes are unchanged but the offsets within the slot differ (address at offset 0, then bool, uint8, bool at offsets 20, 21, 22)
base contract variables get the earliest slots and derived variables continue packing after them, so derivedSmall shares slot 0 with the inherited baseFlag and the uint256 goes to slot 1
